result.title: RISE: Reasoning with Implicit State Embeddings for GUI Agents
result.summary: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents translate user instructions and screenshots into executable actions. To learn executable actions, existing approaches often rely on explicit reasoning during training, which encourage over-reliance on specific reasoning patterns rather than generalizable action-relevant information. In this paper, we propose an implicit framework, RISE, which integrates action-relevant reasoning into implicit state representations to guide GUI action prediction. To this end, action-relevant reasoning is captured through three complementary supervision objectives: full-CoT state alignment preserves information across the reasoning process, action-distribution alignment encodes action preferences, and reasoning-to-action boundary alignment captures the representation immediately before action generation. In this case, our RISE effectively learns informative implicit representations, thereby improving the accuracy of next-action token prediction. RISE achieves 70.6\% accuracy on OSWorld-G, establishing state-of-the-art performance among compared 8B models with a 4.3-point gain over its backbone. Results across two distinct backbones and six diverse benchmarks further demonstrate its effectiveness in GUI grounding and action prediction. Our code is available on our project page.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RISE 框架，将 GUI agent 面向动作的推理压入隐式状态表示，再用全 CoT 状态对齐、动作分布对齐和推理-动作边界对齐三种监督目标训练，以提升下一动作 token 预测准确率，并在多个基准上报告了 8B 规模的最优结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 用隐状态替代显式 CoT 并对其施加多粒度监督，直接对应 LVR 中 latent 状态承载推理内容与训练信号的议题；可供核查其隐表示是否真在推理期被使用、以及三种对齐目标分别贡献了什么。
